name: Shadowhound keeps its absolute HP across a mount/dismount (#9038)
contract: Shadowhound 50124 is a real Pet; Unit::Mount() calls UnsummonPetTemporaryIfAny(), which saves the pet
(SavePetToDB writes the raw curhealth column, no percentage math) and removes it, and dismounting calls
ResummonPetTemporaryUnSummonedIfAny(), which reloads it through Pet::LoadPetFromDB.
Pet::LoadPetFromDB synchronously calls Guardian::InitStatsForLevel (generic, owner-independent stats and
SetFullHealth()) and adds the pet to the map, which synchronously constructs its AI (HoundActions),
scheduling its first EVENT_REFRESH_OWNER tick for 1ms later; the saved absolute health is restored only
later, from an async DB query callback. Instrumentation (temporary LOG_ERROR traces, removed before this
commit) showed the callback's _LoadAuras/CastPetAuras calls raise max health further before the health
column is applied, so the restored absolute health lands against a transient, pre-owner-rescale max
health, not the hound's settled owner-scaled max. HoundActions::Update's EVENT_REFRESH_OWNER handler then
ran its percentage rescale (healthFraction = current/transient-max, newHealth = owner-max * fraction)
on that very first tick, turning the correctly-restored absolute health into a fraction of the wrong
max and losing HP (traced: 100 HP against a transient max of 1545 -> 6.47% -> 57 HP of the correct 894
max) with no combat involved. The fix tracks whether HoundActions has run its owner-refresh correction
before (_ownerRefreshed): on the first correction after (re)construction it clamps the already-correct
absolute health to the new max instead of re-deriving a fraction, and uses the existing proportional
rescale only for later corrections (legitimate owner max-health changes while the hound stays alive). The
fix distinguishes a reload-with-saved-health from a brand-new summon using the exact traced signal: at
HoundActions construction time, Player::GetTemporaryUnsummonedPetNumber() is still nonzero only when this
construction is happening inside Player::ResummonPetTemporaryUnSummonedIfAny() (it is cleared only after
Pet::LoadPetFromDB returns), so only that path is treated as a restore; a brand-new summon never sets it
and keeps filling to the owner-scaled max in full.
Expected: the hound's absolute HP is unchanged by a mount/dismount cycle with no combat (first player), and
a freshly summoned hound (no prior save, second player) starts at its owner-scaled 40%-of-max-health target.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
SETUP: the hunter has a Shadowhound
SETUP: hound at exact absolute 100 HP
Hound HP unchanged across mount/dismount, no combat
A well-geared owner's max health clears the hound's level-locked generic template health
A brand-new Shadowhound (never saved) starts at the owner-scaled 40%-of-max-health target, not a stale generic value
